clue.text: Paid Herbert to delete literal translation

blocks.note: to meet a bill is to pay it, so 'paid' can be 'met'
the initials of A. P. Herbert, the English humorist and MP
an old spelling of raze, meaning to scrape out or erase

explanation.surface: Someone pays a man named Herbert to strike out a word-for-word translation.
explanation.walkthrough: A. P. Herbert was a famous Punch humorist and campaigning MP, so his initials stand in for his surname. RASE is the archaic spelling of raze, to scratch out.
explanation.definitionFit: A metaphrase is a word-for-word rendering from one language into another, as opposed to a paraphrase.

clue.text: One surrounded by, eg draughts in the air

indicators.note: something surrounded by another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: draughts pieces are called men
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Something enclosed by draughts blowing about in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draughts' suggests currents of air, but it is the board game, whose pieces are men. 'Air' means bearing, not atmosphere.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a person's manner or bearing, as is a mien, their look or demeanour.

clue.text: Artist has got rid of an omnivorous monkey

indicators.note: getting rid of something means it is taken away from the word

blocks.note: the Venetian Renaissance painter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter has disposed of a monkey that eats anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Titis are small South American monkeys that eat fruit, leaves, insects and eggs, so their diet is mixed.

clue.text: In a word, not the full address

definitions.note: a phrase meaning a category found in every word, standing for a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: a grammatical class such as noun or verb, which every word is in
second meaning: a section of a talk rather than the whole of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a word' looks like 'briefly'; it points to the grammar label every word carries. An address is a speech, so less than all of it is a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar classes like noun and verb are categories of word, and the phrase literally also means an extract of a talk.

clue.text: Race lacking originality

definitions.note: a noun for something repeated, standing in for an adjective phrase

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to race again
second meaning: a repeat broadcast, nothing new

explanation.definitionFit: To rerun is to run a race again, and a rerun is a repeated programme, which is not fresh or new.

clue.text: Badly cuts about 3 - editor thought to be responsible

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters fall out of order
'about' means going around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
the answer to 3 down taken literally: a part of the word speech
the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor is blamed for clumsy cuts to a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is read literally: the answer to 3 down describes the piece wanted, a part of the word speech, here its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone is suspected of a crime, people think they did it, so they are believed to be to blame.

clue.text: Fish in blue sea, so to speak

indicators.note: 'so to speak' asks for a word by its spoken sound rather than its meaning
'in' places one piece inside the other piece

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling sad
the letter C is pronounced like the word sea

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in the blue sea, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter goes inside the word for blue: S(C)AD.
explanation.definitionFit: The scad is a type of horse mackerel, a small marine food fish.

clue.text: 10 happening at the same time

blocks.note: the answer to 10 across is a company, abbreviated CO
an incident is a happening or event

explanation.surface: A firm event occurring simultaneously.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 across is FIRM, which is a business, so it gives the abbreviation for company.
explanation.definitionFit: Coincident events occur together, simultaneously, so the adjective means happening together in time.

clue.text: Dark as some strange old bloom

indicators.note: something strange is out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unusual order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dark, odd, antique flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The damask rose is an ancient fragrant variety from the Middle East, prized for attar, so an old flower.

clue.text: Undertaking to come in force

blocks.note: to enter is to come in
to prise something open is to force it

explanation.surface: A promise to come in force, like troops arriving in numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a project or venture, something taken on, which is an undertaking.

clue.text: "For who so — that cannot be seduc'd?” asked Cassius

definitions.text: "For who so — that cannot be seduc'd?” asked Cassius

blocks.clueFragment: "For who so — that cannot be seduc'd?” asked Cassius
blocks.note: surface reading: a quotation with one word missing, spoken by a character
setter's reading: the missing word is the one Shakespeare gave Cassius in Julius Caesar, meaning steadfast

explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar, Act 1, Cassius muses that even noble Brutus may be won over: 'For who so firm that cannot be seduced?'
explanation.definitionFit: The blank needs an adjective for someone resolute and unshakeable, which fits the line from the play exactly.

clue.text: Boastful - without result? Splendid!

blocks.note: in vain means without result
glorious means splendid

explanation.surface: A braggart achieves nothing, yet exclaims how splendid it all is.
explanation.definitionFit: Vainglorious describes excessive pride and bragging about one's own achievements.

clue.text: Approves of mugs

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, tolerates or sanctions
second meaning: as a plural noun, faces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mugs' looks like drinking vessels or fools; here it is slang for faces.
explanation.definitionFit: To countenance something is to permit it, and a countenance is a face, which is slangily a mug.

clue.text: How Arnold's armies clashed by night

definitions.text: How Arnold's armies clashed by night

blocks.clueFragment: How Arnold's armies clashed by night
blocks.note: surface reading: a question about some general's night-time battle
setter's reading: Matthew Arnold's poem Dover Beach, where armies clash in the dark without knowledge

explanation.walkthrough: Dover Beach ends 'where ignorant armies clash by night'; the clue asks for the adverb form of that adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's armies fight without knowing who or why, so they clash in a manner lacking knowledge.

clue.text: Staying dry, could Adam get so drunk on his ale?

blocks.note: surface padding that names whose ale is meant, since Adam's ale is a jokey name for water
Adam's ale is water, the only drink in Eden
tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Could the first man get drunk on what he drank and still stay dry?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adam's ale' is an old idiom for plain water. The order is reversed in the clue: 'tight' comes after 'water' in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something watertight lets no liquid in, so its contents stay dry inside it.

clue.text: Plant, damaged, grows last

indicators.note: something damaged is broken out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A damaged plant is the last one to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasswort, or samphire, is a succulent salt-marsh plant once burned to make soda for glassmaking.

clue.text: Attack on the way round - a funny thing

indicators.note: 'round' means going around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
something funny is a laugh

explanation.surface: An assault on someone on their way home, a comic episode.
explanation.definitionFit: An onslaught is a fierce, violent assault, so it is a forceful attack.

clue.text: Bottom position a director holds

indicators.note: the phrase before it holds the answer inside its run of letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: The lowest job in a production is the one a director takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom position' reads as the definition, but only 'Bottom' is; 'position' starts the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the very bottom of something such as fortunes or the sky.

clue.text: Plump for honour points

blocks.note: the Order of the British Empire, a British honour
two compass points, south and east

explanation.surface: Choosing points awarded for honour, as in plumping for an option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' reads as 'choose'; 'Plump' alone is the adjective. The OBE is a British decoration given in the honours lists.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and obese both describe someone carrying a lot of weight, as adjectives.

clue.text: Team having rows - they're just off the field

blocks.note: a side is a team
lines are rows

explanation.surface: A team quarrelling, with players just sent off the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' suggests arguments, but it means lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The sidelines are the boundary areas running alongside a playing pitch, just outside the area of play.

clue.text: Bet dictionary gives “access rooms”

blocks.note: an ante is a stake in poker
Chambers is a well-known British dictionary

explanation.surface: A wager over which dictionary lists a certain phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers is the dictionary favoured by British crossword setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antechambers are small rooms through which one passes to reach a larger room, so they give access.

clue.text: Bother! The point's exploded

blocks.note: 'blow!' is a mild exclamation of annoyance
north, a compass point

explanation.surface: An annoyed cry because the tip has blown off.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing blown up has exploded, so the past participle matches.

clue.text: Go before this singer as Leofric's wife

indicators.note: the word placed in front of this answer is taken off the longer name

blocks.note: taken as written
Lady Godiva, wife of Leofric, Earl of Mercia

explanation.surface: Someone told to make way for a singer posing as a famous noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: Put 'go' in front of the answer and you get Leofric's wife, Lady Godiva, who rode naked through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, a prima donna.

clue.text: Painful thing, with learner out of form

indicators.note: out of means taken away from the word that follows

blocks.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
form and style both mean manner

explanation.surface: A learner driver in poor form finds it painful.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, which hurts.

clue.text: Remaining a republic in Africa

blocks.note: first meaning: still left
second meaning: a West African country

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'to go' means still left to be done, and Togo is the narrow West African republic beside Ghana.

clue.text: Expert at home in any field?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a person, standing for a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: a specialist, here a scientist of soil and crops
second meaning: field read as farmland, so someone comfortable in any crop plot

explanation.walkthrough: 'Any field' sounds like any area of knowledge; the question mark warns it is a literal field of crops.
explanation.definitionFit: This scientist studies soil management and crop production, so is literally comfortable in any agricultural plot.

clue.text: So far, one remains a Tibetan mystery

blocks.note: 'not yet' means not so far
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Up to now, one thing is still an unsolved Himalayan riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a legendary creature of the Himalayas whose existence is unproven.

clue.text: Makes amends – relax in a tranquil state

blocks.note: to atone is to make amends
to ease off is to relax

explanation.surface: Someone apologises and then calms down, at peace with themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at one's ease is an idiom for feeling relaxed and untroubled, which is calm and tranquil.
